name: Finance Prompts
intro: Templates for analysis narratives and board communication. These draft and structure; the numbers and the judgment remain yours, and outputs are not financial advice.

templates.tip: Paste the actual variance table. The model writes the narrative; it must never compute or invent the numbers.
templates.title: Variance analysis narrative
templates.models: Any; verify every figure against the source data.
templates.prompt: Write a variance analysis narrative from the table below. Audience: {CFO_OR_BOARD}. For each line where actual differs from budget by more than {THRESHOLD} percent: state the variance in dollars and percent exactly as shown in the table, give the driver from the notes column, and mark it one-time or recurring. Close with a three-sentence outlook. Do not calculate new figures; use only numbers present in the table. Flag any line where the notes column is empty as UNEXPLAINED. TABLE: {PASTE}

templates.tip: The one-page constraint forces prioritization, which is the actual skill being borrowed.
templates.title: Board-ready financial summary
templates.models: Frontier models hold the no-new-numbers rule more reliably.
templates.prompt: Summarize the attached monthly financials for a board pack. One page maximum. Structure: 1) headline, the single most important development in one sentence; 2) performance vs plan, revenue, gross margin, opex, cash, each one line with the figure from the source; 3) two risks with mitigations; 4) one decision requested from the board, stated as a yes/no question. Use only figures present in the source. Neutral tone, no adjectives before numbers. SOURCE: {PASTE}

templates.tip: Use it before planning meetings; the value is the question list, not answers.
templates.title: Scenario stress questions
templates.prompt: We are planning {PERIOD} for a {INDUSTRY} business with revenue around {REVENUE} and the cost structure summarized here: {SUMMARY}. Generate 12 stress-test questions a rigorous CFO would ask, grouped: demand shocks (4), cost and supply shocks (4), capital and liquidity (4). Each question must name the specific line item at risk and the leading indicator that would give early warning. Do not answer the questions.
